COMMENT: Adds a consequence for civic attention.

SENTENCE: So, the argument is stronger when the benefits can reach local workers and businesses.
COMMENT: Explains the condition for a stronger economic case.

SENTENCE: So, festivals that make both the music scene and also the economy stronger has stronger public support.
COMMENT: Concludes the paragraph's economic point.

SENTENCE: Music festivals face many problems.
COMMENT: Main idea: music festivals face serious environmental and structural problems.

SENTENCE: Leah Thomas (2023) shows that even a well-known festival such as Coachella needs many systems for trash, and reducing plastic pollution needs policy changes.
COMMENT: Provides evidence about environmental strain and policy needs.

SENTENCE: In addition, Jim Ottewill (2026) reports that festivals discussed in the UK Parliament generate 25,800 tonnes of waste, 22,876 tonnes of CO2, and use 185 million litres of water every year.
COMMENT: Adds concrete evidence about waste and emissions.

SENTENCE: The same article offers evidence that improvement is possible: Massive Attack's 2024 Act 1.5 event reduced energy-related greenhouse gas emissions by 98 percent and made an 89 percent recycling rate (Ottewill, 2026).
COMMENT: Adds evidence that improvement is possible.

SENTENCE: Money is also part of the problem, since Oliver (2026) notes that many independent festivals are struggling to survive.
COMMENT: Adds the financial-pressure concern.

SENTENCE: So, festivals should be judged not only by their lineups but also by how seriously organizers address waste, transport, and long-term viability.
COMMENT: Concludes that festivals should be judged by sustainability as well as entertainment.
